Case reference: 2024018918.CaseDesc: Benjamin Sullivan was last seen on February 3rd, 2024 and reported missing on April 21, 2024 from Moncton, New Brunswick.  Benjamin has not been seen or heard from since July 2023. Benjamin is known to live a transient lifestyle and does not have a fixed address. Extensive searches around the city of Moncton, including verifications at shelters and hospitals have been unsuccessful in locating Benjamin.

Case reference: 2017074201.CaseDesc: On August 23, 1995, the remains of an unidentified man were discovered in Lake Ontario, near Cherry Beach, in Toronto, Ontario. Biogeographic ancestry testing predicts he may be of European ancestry.

Case reference: 2006003399.CaseDesc: On November 2, 2001, this male, was found in a sewer at 470 Lansdowne Avenue in Toronto. His ancestry is Caucasian, possibly Egyptian or mixed African/Caucasian. He had previous surgery of his left forearm, which had involved the implant of surgical plates. The numbers visible on the surgical plates could not be traced to a specific individual, however, it was determined that the lot was released some time after May 25, 1994. A MacDonald’s name tag with the name "Raymond" was found in the sewer, which may or may not be related to this individual.

Teeth: Visible Missing, Teeth were stained, which suggests he may have been a smoker,  his upper central incisors were also missing
Fractured/Broken Bones: Left Hip, recent fracture of left hip

Case reference: 2014001088.CaseDesc: On September 13, 1973, the remains of an adult male were recovered from the Whirlpool of the Niagara River, in Niagara Falls. His eye colour is believed to be brown. He was recovered without clothing.

Ring: Silver ring with a green stone on the third finger of his right hand
Watch: Cloth, Left wrist, had a red, yellow and blue watchstrap.

Case reference: 2012020019.CaseDesc: Emerson Dobroskay, was last seen on October 28, 1988 at the Pit Pub located at the University of British Columbia. It is believed that Emerson may have fallen into a large pit dug for construction, but all searches have failed to locate him. Although foul play is not suspected, it cannot be ruled out.

Case reference: 2007003699.CaseDesc: On April 9, 2007, a male was located in a forested area north of the intersection of Fiddlers Green Road and Glancaster Road in the community of Mount Hope, Hamilton. He is believed to have been deceased for 7 to 8 months and possibly longer.

Money: $12.99 with one discolored coin, unknown denomination
Shirt: Denim, Blue, "Kinswood" brand long sleeved button down shirt, size large

Case reference: 2017072253.CaseDesc: On December 8, 2017, at approximately 6:30 a.m., Nadia Atwi was last seen at her residence in north Edmonton, Alberta. Later that day, Nadia's abandoned vehicle was discovered in some bushes on the side of a hill leading into Rundle Park.

Case reference: 2012020025.CaseDesc: At about 8:15 pm on May 3, 1983, 16 year old Shelley-Anne Bacsu left a friend’s house in the Sunset Trailer Park to walk the 7 km to her home. Her route took her west on Highway 16 through Hinton, then north on Highway 40. Witnesses saw Shelley-Anne walking westbound along the shoulder of Highway 16 carrying her school books; she was not hitch-hiking. Shelley-Anne was last seen in the area of what was then the western edge of town. A dark colored van was seen in the area around the time Shelley-Anne was walking home, some reports were that it was stopped at the side of the road near where she was last seen. An extensive search for the van and/or its occupants was not successful. Several days after Shelley-Anne was last seen, some of her belongings were found near the Athabasca River not far from the outskirts of Hinton.

Case reference: 2005005699.CaseDesc: On June 22, 1991, the body of an unidentified man was recovered from the Niagara River between Horseshoe Falls and the "Maid of the Mist" boat docks. His post-mortem weight was recorded as being 113 lbs, however this measurement may not represent his actual living weight due to post-mortem changes noted at autopsy. He had signs of having suffered an acute or chronic right lung infection. He is estimated to have been dead for several months. Biogeographic Ancestry testing predicts this unidentified male is either of European ancestry, or South Asian ancestry, or mixed European and South Asian ancestry.

Teeth: Several amalgam fillings in his teeth and multiple posterior teeth in his upper and lower jaw were lost/removed prior to death.

Case reference: 2006013699.CaseDesc: Emile Morissette was last seen while on a fishing trip at Birch Lake in Timmins Township, Ontario on July 6, 1976.

Case reference: 2014006326.CaseDesc: Ronald Kay was reported missing to the Regina Police Service on November 26, 2013. He was last seen at the Saskatchewan Rough Riders Football game and has not been seen since.

Shoes: Red, Sneakers, Sneakers made of suede
Scar: Ears, Piercing scar on left ear

Hat: Black, Baseball hat-" Detroit Red Wings"

Shoes: Canvas, Black, White, Running shoes, brand "Adidas"

Case reference: 2026007673.CaseDesc: Toward the end of November 2025, Roger Rochon was last seen in Joliette, Quebec, as he was getting ready to take the bus to Toronto, Ontario. Case reference: 2023025594.CaseDesc: On September 17, 2010, Tiamanja Palazzo was last observed in close proximity to the American Falls, in Niagara Falls, New York, USA. Case reference: 2015026912.CaseDesc: On May 25, 2015, Kandice Singbeil was seen for the last time by her boyfriend in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan.

Case reference: 2014001248.CaseDesc: William Roy Tennant left his home in the Municipality of Leamington, Ontario, on October 5, 1990. William was reported missing on October 9th, 1990, by his sister, who was concerned about his mental health.

Case reference: 2014001425.CaseDesc: Terry Hrynick was reported missing by the manager of Sickle Lake Lodge in Manitoba in the early hours of August 3, 1986. He had spent the previous evening and early morning with friends. According to them, Terry had been very quiet in the days leading up to his disappearance. On the night of his disappearance, he was described as intoxicated. At one point, witnesses saw him stumble out the door of the cabin. About 15 minutes later, they heard a boat but did not see him. The empty boat was located the following day. An extensive search on land and water failed to find him. There was no indication that Terry found his way to shore and he has not been seen since.

Case reference: 2012020165.CaseDesc: The remains of this male were found in a forested area immediately north of the Port Coquitlam cemetery.

Teeth: Visible Decay, Missing an upper front tooth on the left side prior to death. The upper front tooth on the right side was angled.
Deformity: Left Knee, Osgoode-Schlatter's disease - bony bump on shin below knee

Case reference: 2013000090.CaseDesc: On June 16, 1983, Nicola Michel Tola was seen for the last time in Montreal, Quebec. He was suppose to come home and make dinner but he was never seen again by his family. His car was located at the Pie IX shopping mall.

Case reference: 2014002145.CaseDesc: On September 13, 1975, William Garson, his father, his brother and a friend set out for a hunt in Moose Lake, Manitoba. On September 14, other hunters found gas cans and a thermos with the Garson name on it. These hunters reported their findings to the police.  A search was initiated and police found a boat sitting upright on the bottom of the lake. The depth of the lake around the boat was only 8 to 10 feet. Police believe the men encountered extremely rough water while crossing Moose Lake. The motors were found to be in forward gear. There was no flotation gear in the boat and it was heavily loaded with camping and hunting equipment. All bodies recovered except William, presumed drowned.

Case reference: 2018059815.CaseDesc: Leroy Custer was last seen in Prince Albert, Saskatchewan, on August 30, 2018.

Case reference: 2006004799.CaseDesc: Ralph Monague and Curtis Smith were passengers on the Christian Island Ferry travelling between Cedar Point and Christian Island on December 22, 1985, when they fell over board in stormy conditions.

Case reference: 2014003840.CaseDesc: On December 7, 1986, a male was seen floating in the river. The male initially responded to police calls however shortly after he was observed going under the water. It is presumed he drowned. The identity of the male was unknown to police until Roderick Cook's parents contacted police advising they had not seen their son for some time. It is assumed the man in the river was Roderick based both on the description and the fact that he was seen walking near the river. Police further found footprints that led from the shore to the open water. No foul play is suspected in this matter and it is assumed Roderick drowned.

Teeth: Two front upper teeth are false

Case reference: 2014006747.CaseDesc: Jian Ping Li and her 6 month old baby, Xiao Feng Lu, were last seen at their family residence around 9:40 a.m in Brossard, Quebec on April 30, 2014.  When her husband returned that day, around 2:30 p.m., there was nobody home and the back door was unlocked.  Jian Ping Li's car was still at the residence, however she left without her purse, wallet, credit card, cell phone, money, as well as the diaper bag, the stroller and the car seat for the baby.

A pair of nail clippers was also found nearby. His death is estimated to have occurred in the spring or summer prior.

Case reference: 2014003848.CaseDesc: On November 5, 1964, the Grand Rapids RCMP were advised that Harvey Hudson was two weeks overdue in returning from a trip to Cedar Lake from Grand Rapids, Manitoba. It was established that Harvey left The Pas on October 20th and arrived at the Cedar Lake Post.  When he reached Cedar Lake, he was told to wait for a boat from Easterville which was expected shortly. A witness said he walked to Easterville but turned back. He then took a canoe and set off for Easterville, using a piece of board as a paddle. It is believed that Harvey had little or no food, rifle or other camping supplies. Numerous land, air and water patrols were made with negative results.

The Slocan Lake RCMP are very concerned for Thierry's health and well-being and are encouraging the public to contact police if they know his current whereabouts or have seen him. It is out of character for Thierry to be missing for so long.

Case reference: 2014004217.CaseDesc: On May 7, 1968, Bernice Redhead and her family were travelling on a dog sled led by their grandfather. The group was travelling on Gods River, Shamattawa, Manitoba, when they broke through the ice. All the passengers fell into the water. The grandfather managed to pull everyone to safety, except for Bernice, who was swept away by the river's fast-moving current. She has not been found to this day.

He has evidence of heart disease and may have had heart problems in the past. It is estimated that he had been in the water for a few days up to two weeks prior to discovery. Biogeographic Ancestry testing predicts that this unidentified male is of European ancestry.

Hair: Brown, Grey, Long, Long grey and white beard 12cm
Teeth: No upper teeth and no lower posterior teeth; remaining teeth have roots only; crowns are lost due to decay.

Case reference: 2017040839.CaseDesc: Claude Lévesque was last seen on July 17, 2017, in the Mercier/Hochelaga-Maisonneuve sector of Montreal, Quebec. Claude had an appointment with his doctor that afternoon, but he never showed up. Claude was known to be despondent.

Case reference: 2008003299.CaseDesc: On May 17, 1985, Cyril Cheong was fishing on White Lake with his friends when the weather deteriorated and strong winds started to blow. Case reference: 2014003434.CaseDesc: On the evening of May 18, 1986, Monique Brosseau was seen for the last time at her home in Duhamel-Ouest, Quebec.

Case reference: 2014002923.CaseDesc: On March 27, 1998, Jacqueline Olynyk was witnessed walking along the Red River in Winnipeg, Manitoba. We have not received any communication or sightings of Jacqueline since that day.

Case reference: 2007004899.CaseDesc: James Gordon MacDonald was last seen by his father on October 23, 1980 in Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario. An extensive investigation by the Sault Ste Marie Police Service was conducted but to this date James has not been seen or heard from since.

Case reference: 2011005799.CaseDesc: On June 20, 2011 Ibrahim Sendagire was driving on Highway 17 between Terrace Bay and Marathon, Ontario.  He was involved in a motor vehicle accident and fled the scene into the bush area. Police searches of the area yielded negative results. Ibrahim has not been located and has had no contact with family or friends. Last Seen: Highway 17, Tuuri Township.  Approximately 4 km west of the Steel River bridge near Black Fox Lake.  This area is essentially located between the towns of Marathon and Terrace Bay, in Northwestern Ontario.

Case reference: 2014002565.CaseDesc: On July 5, 1975, Carl Gallen was employed as a steelworker on the Long Spruce Dam project. He and his partner were working on a cement wall near the river. Carl was drilling into the wall when he fell into the water. His partner stated that he went directly under the water and did not see him surface. Carl wasn't wearing a harness or lifejacket. It's presumed he drowned.

Case reference: 2020028363.CaseDesc: On July 20, 2020, around 9:00 a.m., Sumira Rashid was seen for the last time in Montreal, Quebec when she left her family home. Sumira left home with a sports bag under the pretext of going shopping but she never returned and has not been seen since. An investigation concluded that Sumira later took a flight to Los Angeles, California.

Case reference: 2016067951.CaseDesc: On October 15, 2016, Eric Ratt was last seen canoeing approximately 70 km east of the MacArthur River to Sandy Lake (Points North area), Saskatchewan. He has cabins at Sandy Lake and was traveling alone up the Geike River with approximately three weeks of supplies. Eric was reported missing after failing to pick up supplies from a pre-arranged location.

Case reference: 2020007795.CaseDesc: On November 15, 1972, at around midnight, James Edwards was last seen in his Toronto Transit Commission (TTC) uniform leaving for work in Toronto, Ontario. TTC advised that James had submitted his resignation before his disappearance.

Case reference: 2014001410.CaseDesc: Emma Dixon was last seen on July 22, 1964 at her home on Union Bar Reserve, in Hope, British Columbia. Her husband said that she may have gone to Washington for work. Emma never told anyone she was leaving and did not take any personal belongings. She was reported missing on August 20, 1964.

Case reference: 2014002821.CaseDesc: On the weekend of August 18, 1972, Dennis Simpson and a friend went fishing on McMillian Lake in Manitoba. When they did not return by the 22nd, many people contacted the police. Through investigation, it was later determined that the two men were last seen by a man on the shore on Sunday the 20th, and their camp was still set up. They told the person that they were going to make one more pass and then break camp. The weather conditions at the time were such that there would have been rough water. Given this, and the fact that the men were in a relatively small canoe, it was determined that they may have capsized. An extensive search by land, water and air failed to find anything other than various items identified as belonging to the two missing fishermen. Dennis was never found.

Case reference: 2014004389.CaseDesc: On October 23, 2003, Bertha Melvin, a resident of a group home, left a note saying she was going to hospital. However, she failed to attend.  Bertha is described as very introverted and may have been frequenting urban areas and the Waterways neighbourhood in Fort McMurray, Alberta.
